lineage: Robustness check on the v2 pooled co-occupancy result (results/spatial_occupancy_v2.json, MSLNxCA9 and MSLNxPSCA). The v1/v2 shifted-null verdicts are unchanged and stay on record. Designed after seeing v2 outcomes, so it is a robustness check, not an independent test.
question: Is the observed co-occupancy explained by spot sequencing depth? Positivity is count>0, which rises with total UMI per spot; two genes can look co-occupying simply because both are detected in deep spots.
data: Lane B features_cache counts_sparse, px, genes (same 68 sections, same ENSG map, same MIN_POS=10 and positivity rule as scripts_spatial_occupancy.py). Per-spot depth = row sum of counts_sparse.
null: Depth-stratified permutation: spots are split into 5 quantile bins of total counts within each section; for each of 1000 draws, gene2 positivity is permuted within bins (gene1 fixed). Jaccard recomputed. seed 20261008. Per-section empirical p_co=(#null>=obs+1)/(1001), effect = observed Jaccard - null median.
endpoints: Same as v2: paired Wilcoxon (two-sided) of effect vs 0 across qualifying sections, Fisher combination of per-section p_co, median effect with 95% bootstrap CI (10000 section resamples).
gate: A target pair (MSLNxCA9, MSLNxPSCA) SURVIVES if Wilcoxon p<0.05 AND Fisher p<0.05 AND median effect>0, AND all three positive controls (ERBB2xTACSTD2, ERBB2xMUC1, SLC39A6xCA12) pass the same rule. Otherwise the pair does NOT survive the depth control and is reported as such, alongside the v2 result.
limits_declared: Within-bin permutation ignores spatial autocorrelation, so it is anti-conservative as a spatial null by itself; it is a depth control and complements, not replaces, the shifted null. Depth is a proxy for technical confounding only; no tumor-purity or cell-type control. HER2-positive cohort, same sections as v1/v2.
not_done: No outcome computed when this file was written.
